items.prompt: A function must return every distinct value. It builds a set of distinct values and then copies those values into a separate result array. If there are d distinct values, how should the two structures be classified?

options.text: The set is O(d) auxiliary space and the returned array is O(d) output space.
Both structures are output space because they contain the same values.
Both structures are auxiliary space because they are created during execution.
The set is output space and the returned array is auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Classification follows each structure's role, not whether it contains similar data.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “The set is O(d) auxiliary space and the returned array is O(d) output space.”. The set is temporary state used to construct the required result. The separate returned array is the output. Both scale with d, but they belong to different accounting categories.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Classification follows each structure's role, not whether it contains similar data.
Why the other choices fail

items: Both structures are output space because they contain the same values. — The temporary set is not returned or otherwise part of the required result.
Both structures are auxiliary space because they are created during execution. — The returned array is required output and should not be counted as temporary working memory.
The set is output space and the returned array is auxiliary space. — This reverses the actual roles of the two structures.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_output: The temporary set is not returned or otherwise part of the required result.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_auxiliary: The returned array is required output and should not be counted as temporary working memory.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.set_output_array_aux: This reverses the actual roles of the two structures.

items.prompt: A function builds a map of value frequencies and returns that same map as its required result. It uses no other growing structure. Which classification is most precise?

options.text: The map is O(d) output space; auxiliary space outside the returned map is O(1).
The map is O(d) auxiliary space and output space is O(1).
The map is both O(d) output space and O(d) auxiliary space.
Both output and auxiliary space are O(1) because each update is constant time.

feedback.reason: A structure created during execution can still be output space when it is the required returned result.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “The map is O(d) output space; auxiliary space outside the returned map is O(1).”. The map stores one entry per distinct value and is returned directly. It therefore represents O(d) output storage. Constant-time updates do not imply constant memory.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: A structure created during execution can still be output space when it is the required returned result.
Why the other choices fail

items: The map is O(d) auxiliary space and output space is O(1). — The map is not temporary; it is the required result.
The map is both O(d) output space and O(d) auxiliary space. — One structure should not be counted in both categories merely because it was built incrementally.
Both output and auxiliary space are O(1) because each update is constant time. — Per-operation time says nothing about the final number of stored entries.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.map_is_auxiliary: The map is not temporary; it is the required result.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.map_counts_twice: One structure should not be counted in both categories merely because it was built incrementally.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_constant: Per-operation time says nothing about the final number of stored entries.

items.prompt: A function returns the prefix-sum array for an input of length n and writes each prefix sum directly into the returned array. It uses one running total. Which statement is correct?

options.text: O(n) output space and O(1) auxiliary space.
O(1) output space and O(n) auxiliary space.
O(n) output space and O(n) auxiliary space because the result is built incrementally.
O(1) output space and O(1) auxiliary space because only one pass is used.

feedback.reason: The returned prefix array is output, while the running total is constant working state.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “O(n) output space and O(1) auxiliary space.”. The algorithm materializes n result values. Building the result one element at a time does not turn that required output into auxiliary space.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: The returned prefix array is output, while the running total is constant working state.
Why the other choices fail

items: O(1) output space and O(n) auxiliary space. — The n-element returned array is output, not auxiliary memory.
O(n) output space and O(n) auxiliary space because the result is built incrementally. — The output array should not also be charged as temporary state.
O(1) output space and O(1) auxiliary space because only one pass is used. — One pass does not make an n-element result constant-size.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.output_1_aux_n: The n-element returned array is output, not auxiliary memory.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_n: The output array should not also be charged as temporary state.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_1: One pass does not make an n-element result constant-size.

items.prompt: Which structures should be counted as output space? Select all that apply.

options.text: A newly allocated array that is the required returned list of distinct values.
A frequency map that is returned as the required result.
A seen set discarded after producing a separate boolean result.
A normalized copy discarded after two inputs are compared.

feedback.reason: Output space consists of storage that directly represents the required result.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “A newly allocated array that is the required returned list of distinct values.”, “A frequency map that is returned as the required result.”. Returned collections are output when the contract requires their contents. Temporary sets and normalized copies are auxiliary when they are discarded after computing another result.

blocks.title: Decision rule

items.prompt: A one-pass algorithm appends every retained element to a new result array. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The time may be O(n), while output space can still be O(k) for k retained elements.
One pass guarantees O(1) output and auxiliary space.
The result array is always auxiliary because it is created inside the loop.
Appending any number of elements necessarily makes time O(n²).

feedback.reason: Pass count determines traversal work, not the size of the required result.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “The time may be O(n), while output space can still be O(k) for k retained elements.”. A linear scan can construct an output whose size grows with the number of retained elements. The result array remains output space even though it is populated during execution.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Pass count determines traversal work, not the size of the required result.
Why the other choices fail

items: One pass guarantees O(1) output and auxiliary space. — A single traversal can still materialize a large result.
The result array is always auxiliary because it is created inside the loop. — A structure's role is determined by the contract, not by where it is allocated.
Appending any number of elements necessarily makes time O(n²). — Appending does not inherently require scanning the existing output on every operation.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.result_array_is_auxiliary: A structure's role is determined by the contract, not by where it is allocated.

Both the boolean and the set are output space.
Both are O(1) because set membership is expected O(1).

feedback.reason: The boolean is the required result, while the seen set is discarded working state.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “O(1) output space and O(d) auxiliary space.”. The set may grow to d entries, so auxiliary space is O(d). Expected O(1) membership is an operation-cost statement, not a bound on total stored state.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: The boolean is the required result, while the seen set is discarded working state.
Why the other choices fail

items: O(d) output space and O(1) auxiliary space. — The set is not returned, while the boolean is the required output.
Both the boolean and the set are output space. — Temporary diagnostic state is not part of the output contract.
Both are O(1) because set membership is expected O(1). — Constant expected lookup time does not imply a constant number of stored keys.

items.prompt: Which structures should be counted as auxiliary space? Select all that apply.

options.text: A seen set used to compute a boolean and discarded before return.
A copied array sorted only to help compare two inputs, then discarded.
The array explicitly required and returned by the function.
The caller-provided input array.

feedback.reason: Auxiliary space is extra working memory that is neither pre-existing input nor required result storage.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “A seen set used to compute a boolean and discarded before return.”, “A copied array sorted only to help compare two inputs, then discarded.”. The temporary set and copied array support computation and are discarded. The returned array is output, while the original array is input storage.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Auxiliary space is extra working memory that is neither pre-existing input nor required result storage.

items: The array explicitly required and returned by the function. — Required result storage is output space rather than auxiliary memory.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly compare storage strategies for producing a filtered sequence? Select all that apply.

options.text: Writing the logical result into the input prefix can avoid a growing additional output container.
Appending directly to the returned array uses output space without requiring a separate temporary list.
Building a temporary list and then copying it into a returned array adds growing auxiliary space.
Implementations returning equal values must use the same auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Output equivalence does not determine whether an implementation materializes temporary state.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “Writing the logical result into the input prefix can avoid a growing additional output container.”, “Appending directly to the returned array uses output space without requiring a separate temporary list.”, “Building a temporary list and then copying it into a returned array adds growing auxiliary space.”. In-place reuse, direct output construction, and temporary-then-copy strategies can produce the same values with different storage roles and peaks.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Output equivalence does not determine whether an implementation materializes temporary state.
Why the other choices fail

items: Implementations returning equal values must use the same auxiliary space. — Equal results do not imply equal implementation memory.

items.prompt: A function returns an empty array when every input value is filtered out, but its implementation first copies all n values into a temporary buffer. Which statement is precise for that input?

options.text: Output space is O(1) for the empty result, but auxiliary space is O(n) because of the temporary buffer.
Both output and auxiliary space are O(1) because the returned array is empty.
Output space is O(n) and auxiliary space is O(1).
Auxiliary space is O(n) only because the original input has n values.

feedback.reason: Output size and temporary allocation size can differ substantially on the same execution.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “Output space is O(1) for the empty result, but auxiliary space is O(n) because of the temporary buffer.”. The required result contains no elements, but the implementation still allocates a full temporary copy. That copy is auxiliary because it is discarded rather than returned.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Output size and temporary allocation size can differ substantially on the same execution.
Why the other choices fail

items: Both output and auxiliary space are O(1) because the returned array is empty. — A small result does not erase large temporary allocations.
Output space is O(n) and auxiliary space is O(1). — The n-element buffer is temporary, while the returned result is empty.
Auxiliary space is O(n) only because the original input has n values. — The original input is not auxiliary; the newly allocated copy is.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_constant: A small result does not erase large temporary allocations.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.linear_output_only: The n-element buffer is temporary, while the returned result is empty.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.input_counts_as_aux: The original input is not auxiliary; the newly allocated copy is.

items.prompt: A function emits each retained value to a caller-provided stream as soon as it is found and keeps only constant local state. Which statement is most precise?

options.text: It produces k output values while using O(1) auxiliary space without materializing all k values internally.
It has no output because no array is returned.
The emitted values count as O(k) auxiliary space inside the function.
Output size is O(1) because values are emitted one at a time.

feedback.reason: Streaming can avoid materializing the full result while the logical output still contains k values.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “It produces k output values while using O(1) auxiliary space without materializing all k values internally.”. The function's internal working memory remains constant. Output size describes the amount produced, whereas materialized output storage depends on the interface and accounting convention.

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: Streaming can avoid materializing the full result while the logical output still contains k values.
Why the other choices fail

items: It has no output because no array is returned. — Producing values through a stream is still output behavior even without returning an array.
The emitted values count as O(k) auxiliary space inside the function. — Values already handed to the output sink are not retained as the function's working memory.
Output size is O(1) because values are emitted one at a time. — Emitting one item at a time does not reduce the total number of output items.

blocks.text: How to reason it out

The correct choice is “Both use O(k) output space, but B uses O(k) more auxiliary space for the temporary list.”. Each implementation returns a k-element array, so output space is O(k). B additionally retains a separate temporary k-element list before copying, which contributes O(k) auxiliary space.
